entries.title: I Kings 3:2
segments:
Only the people sacrificed; the word "only" implies that in general the people were obedient to the law of Moses, but that in this respect they did not comply it. 
 
  In high places; the high places where the people sacrificed, as here, to Jehovah, must be distinguished from the high places devoted to the worship of idols.  The law of Moses required that all offerings should be made at the tabernacle,
; but previously to the building of the temple this rule was not strictly observed, even by such eminent prophets as Samuel,

entries.title: I Kings 3:3
segments: To love God is the highest duty, the greatest honor, and the supreme blessedness of men.  Those who do it, whatever their condition in this world, are kings and priests unto God, and will reign with him for ever and ever.

entries.title: I Kings 3:5
segments:
A dream; before men had the Bible to guide them, God sometimes made known to them his will in dreams. 
 
The fact that before the canon of Scripture was complete, God sometimes made known his will in dreams, gives no countenance to the idea that he continues to do it, or that any can safely be guided by dreams now.

entries.title: I Kings 3:6
segments: God in not only permitting, but inviting all in every condition who lack wisdom to ask it of him in faith and love, expecting on the ground of his promise to receive it, shows marvellous condescension and kindness; and if any to whom his is revealed do not become wise unto salvation, it will be their own fault.

entries.title: I Kings 3:7
segments:
A little child; young and inexperienced. 
 
  Go out or come in; act as ruler in Israel. 
 
A deep sense of want and a grateful recognition of the goodness of God, confidence in his willingness and power to help, and a disposition to ask of him, are a good preparation for receiving what we need.

entries.title: I Kings 3:10
segments: God is pleased when men from the heart ask for wisdom to understand and do their duty; and in all such cases he will give them not only what they ask, but numerous other blessings for this world and the world to come.

entries.title: I Kings 3:11
segments: Discern judgment; judge rightly in cases that might come before him.

entries.title: I Kings 3:14
segments: Lengthen thy days; this and other promises made to Solomon were on condition that he should continue to obey God.

Obedience to God is conducive to health, long life, and the greatest enjoyment of temporal favors.  It is also conducive to the greatest usefulness, and is, through divine grace, a sure preparation for heaven.

entries.title: I Kings 3:22
segments: Persons who steal will also lie, and the practice of these sins prepares the heart for, and often leads to the commission of murder.

entries.title: I Kings 3:23
segments: An acquaintance with human nature, and with the working of the various passions of the human heart, is an important qualification for a judge, and will in various ways aid him in eliciting evidence and coming to right decisions.

entries.title: I Kings 3:26
segments: A mother's love is great and in high degree self-denying, but the practice of iniquity tends to destroy it, and to sink the mind to such baseness as to wish to rob others of what it cannot itself enjoy.

entries.title: I Kings 3:27
segments: She is the mother; having shown for the child a mother's love.
